dataLineageViz.maxNodes.markdownDescription: Maximum database objects loaded into the graph (10–5000). A selection over the limit is refused; select fewer schemas or raise this setting.

dataLineageViz.renderLimit.markdownDescription: Maximum rendered nodes before showing a warning instead of the graph. Prevents browser performance issues with very large visualizations.

dataLineageViz.excludePatterns.markdownDescription: Regex patterns that exclude objects from the graph when a source is opened (e.g. `_TEST$`, `^staging\\.`). Matched against `schema.object`; `%` is accepted as a wildcard. Requires reloading the data source.

dataLineageViz.externalRefs.enabled.markdownDescription: Detect external references (OPENROWSET file paths, cross-database 3-part names). When disabled, no virtual external nodes are created. External Tables are unaffected. Requires reloading the data source to take effect.

dataLineageViz.overview.enabled.markdownDescription: Enable Schema View. When a loaded graph exceeds `overview.threshold` nodes it starts in schema-level cluster nodes; otherwise in Object View.

dataLineageViz.overview.threshold.markdownDescription: Node count above which the graph starts in Schema View; at or below it starts in Object View. Evaluated on initial load and Refresh View.

enumDescriptions: Double-clicking a schema adds it to Expanded Schema View.
Double-clicking a schema makes it the only expanded schema.
dataLineageViz.overview.schemaDoubleClic.markdownDescription: Controls what double-clicking a schema node does in Schema View. `expand` adds the schema to Expanded Schema View; `expandOnly` makes the clicked schema the only expanded schema.

dataLineageViz.parseRulesFile.markdownDescription: Path to a custom parse rules YAML file. Leave empty for built-in defaults. [Customization guide](https://github.com/ChrisDevRepo/vscode_data_lineage/blob/main/docs/PARSE_RULES.md)

dataLineageViz.dmvQueryTimeout.markdownDescription: Timeout (seconds) per DMV query. Increase for large databases.

dataLineageViz.dmvQueriesFile.markdownDescription: Path to a custom DMV queries YAML file. Leave empty for built-in defaults. [Customization guide](https://github.com/ChrisDevRepo/vscode_data_lineage/blob/main/docs/DMV_QUERIES.md)

enumDescriptions: Use connections saved in the SQL Server (mssql) extension. Microsoft is retiring this API.
Connect directly with Data Lineage's own connections (SQL login or Microsoft Entra ID). Passwords stay in the VS Code secret store.
dataLineageViz.database.connectionProvid.markdownDescription: Where database connections come from. With `builtIn`, add connections with **Data Lineage: Add Database Connection**.

dataLineageViz.database.connections.markdownDescription:
Built-in database connections. Passwords are kept in VS Code secure storage.

**Manage:** [Add](command:dataLineageViz.addDatabaseConnection) · [Edit](command:dataLineageViz.editDatabaseConnection) · [Update Password](command:dataLineageViz.updateDatabasePassword) · [Remove](command:dataLineageViz.removeDatabaseConnection)

id.markdownDescription: Stable identifier; also names the secret-store entry of the password.

database.description: Database to open. Leave empty to choose at connect time.

authenticationType.description: Sign-in type. Windows authentication is not supported.
enumDescriptions: SQL Server login with user name and password.
Microsoft Entra ID sign-in through VS Code.

accountId.description: Id of the Microsoft account in VS Code to sign in with.

tenantId.description: Microsoft Entra tenant id to sign in to.

trustServerCertificate.description: Trust the server certificate without validation. Use only for servers you control.

dataLineageViz.tableStatistics.enabled.markdownDescription: Show column statistics and row counts in the table design viewer (database import only).

dataLineageViz.tableStatistics.standardM.markdownDescription: Allow **Standard** profiling mode (adds MIN/MAX, string length range, AVG, STDEV, zero/empty counts). When `false`, only Quick mode is available — lighter queries.

dataLineageViz.tableStatistics.excludeEx.markdownDescription: Skip profiling for external tables. External tables query remote data sources (S3, Blob, other databases) — profiling can be slow and expensive.

dataLineageViz.tableStatistics.sampleThr.markdownDescription: Advanced: Tables above this row count use sampling instead of a full scan. Set to `0` to always sample.

dataLineageViz.tableStatistics.sampleSiz.markdownDescription: Advanced: Number of rows to sample when profiling large tables.

dataLineageViz.tableStatistics.useApprox.markdownDescription: Advanced: Use `APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT` instead of exact `COUNT(DISTINCT)`. Much faster with ~2% margin. Requires SQL Server 2019+.

dataLineageViz.tableStatistics.maxColumn.markdownDescription: Advanced: Maximum number of columns to profile per table. Columns beyond this cap are skipped. Prevents massive queries on wide tables.

dataLineageViz.layout.direction.markdownDescription: Direction of the dependency graph layout.

enumDescriptions: Smooth step edges with rounded corners

dataLineageViz.layout.edgeAnimation.markdownDescription: Animate edges when running a trace.

dataLineageViz.layout.highlightAnimation.markdownDescription: Animate edges when clicking a node.

dataLineageViz.layout.minimapEnabled.markdownDescription: Show the graph minimap for navigation.

dataLineageViz.layout.rankSeparation.markdownDescription: Advanced: Horizontal spacing between dependency layers (pixels).

dataLineageViz.layout.nodeSeparation.markdownDescription: Advanced: Vertical spacing between nodes in the same layer (pixels).

dataLineageViz.trace.defaultUpstreamLeve.markdownDescription: How many levels upstream (inputs) to trace by default.

dataLineageViz.trace.defaultDownstreamLe.markdownDescription: How many levels downstream (outputs) to trace by default.

dataLineageViz.analysis.hubMinDegree.markdownDescription: Minimum number of connections for an object to appear in the hub list.

dataLineageViz.analysis.islandMaxSize.markdownDescription: Max connected component size to qualify as an island. Higher values include larger disconnected subgraphs; set lower (e.g. 5) to focus on small isolated pairs/groups only.

dataLineageViz.analysis.longestPathMinNo.markdownDescription: Minimum number of objects in a dependency chain for longest-path analysis.

dataLineageViz.mcp.enabled.markdownDescription: Serve the lineage tools to MCP clients on `127.0.0.1`. Bearer-token protected; tools read the project loaded in the Data Lineage panel and never execute SQL. A kill switch: while off, none of the MCP code loads; turning it on takes effect after a window reload, and turning it off stops the server at once and revokes its token. Use *Data Lineage: Copy MCP Client Configuration* to connect a client.

dataLineageViz.mcp.port.markdownDescription: Local TCP port of the MCP server. One VS Code window can serve a port at a time.

dataLineageViz.ai.enabled.description: Enable the @lineage chat participant and its VS Code language-model tools. Disable for users who do not use VS Code Copilot or want to remove them. The MCP server has its own switch, dataLineageViz.mcp.enabled (off by default).

dataLineageViz.ai.maxRounds.markdownDescription: Maximum rounds per `@lineage` deep analysis. Each procedure, view or function it reads takes one round. Read on every request.

dataLineageViz.ai.maxTraceColumns.markdownDescription: Maximum starting columns one `@lineage` column trace may follow. Read on every request.

dataLineageViz.ai.discoveryNodeCap.markdownDescription: Maximum scope nodes the AI may pull in a single discovery-phase catalog request before it escalates to a deep analysis that needs your approval.

dataLineageViz.ai.discoveryTokenBudget.markdownDescription: Maximum estimated DDL tokens for a single discovery-phase catalog request, further capped at one eighth of the selected model's input window. Exceeding it escalates to a deep analysis that needs your approval.

dataLineageViz.ai.outputTemplateFile.markdownDescription:
Path to custom AI output templates YAML. Controls how `@lineage` formats summary, description, badges, highlights, and notes. Leave empty for built-in defaults. Use Command Palette → *Create AI Output Templates* to scaffold. [Customization guide](https://github.com/ChrisDevRepo/vscode_data_lineage/blob/main/docs/AI_PROMPTS.md)

All settings are described in the [settings reference](https://github.com/ChrisDevRepo/vscode_data_lineage/blob/main/docs/FEATURES.md#settings-reference).

languageModelTools.name: lineage_get_context
languageModelTools.userDescription: Shows what is currently loaded and visible in the lineage graph.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns the current database context including loaded schemas, stats, and active UI filters.

languageModelTools.name: lineage_search_objects
languageModelTools.userDescription: Search for database objects by name or column.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Search database objects by name or column (substring or regex). Returns object IDs, metadata, per-kind `by_type` counts, `in_user_filter`, and `name_match` (`unique` or `ambiguous` ids for an exact name, in-filter first). When an in-filter search is empty but out-of-filter hits exist, widen `schemas` on the next call. Use lineage_search_ddl to grep SQL bodies.

query.description: In substring mode: any part of an object or column name, without a schema prefix like '[dbo].'. In regex mode: the pattern, used verbatim. May be empty ONLY together with schemas[] to list everything in those schemas.

schemas.description: Optional schema-name filter; combine with a zero-length query to list objects in those schemas.

mode.description: Name matching strategy: "substring" (default) or "regex" (case-insensitive, matched against name and schema.name).

cursor.description: Page cursor: the next_cursor of the previous result, sent unchanged to read the next page of the same list. Omit for the first page.

languageModelTools.name: lineage_get_scope_bundle
languageModelTools.userDescription: Get a bounded BFS scope in one call, with optional DDL for all nodes in scope.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Graph-scope retrieval for multi-object lineage questions. In `nodes[]`, the origin carries `in` (writes INTO it) and `out` (reads FROM it); every node carries `uh`/`dh`, its hop distance upstream/downstream from the origin on the side(s) it was reached (the origin is 0 on both; a node reached on both sides carries both) — read this instead of re-deriving reach from edge order. `edges` are positional [source, target, type]. Set include_ddl=true when the user wants scope logic. Keep lineage_get_object_detail for one object.

origin.description: Canonical object ID at the center of the requested lineage scope.

upstream_depth.description: Upstream levels: a positive integer, "all" for the whole chain, or 0 to exclude upstream. Use the smallest depth that answers the question: 1 for direct neighbours; "all" only for a whole-chain or path question.

downstream_depth.description: Downstream levels: a positive integer, "all" for the whole chain, or 0 to exclude downstream. Use the smallest depth that answers the question: 1 for direct neighbours; "all" only for a whole-chain or path question.

include_ddl.description: Whether to include SQL bodies for nodes in the returned scope.

languageModelTools.name: lineage_present_result
languageModelTools.userDescription: Generate a report and visualization for the current lineage scope.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Renders a lineage view in the Data Lineage panel: required report sections, node badges, notes, and graph role/color highlights such as source/transform/target. A follow-up render may also prune or add nodes. Returns success with the view name and node count; a rejection names the field to correct. Use this for presentation-only changes.

name.description: Short name for the generated lineage view — aim for ~60 chars.

summary.description: One-line summary shown with the generated view.

intro.description: Optional grounded introduction to the final report.

prune_node_ids.description: Ids to remove from the view. The origin stays, and every remaining node must stay connected to it.

add_node_ids.description: Ids to add to the view; each must connect to it.

label.description: Short legend label for the shared graph role or status.

color.description: Flow role or status. `source`: the deepest origins whose data feeds the answer. `target`: where the data lands — the queried object in an upstream trace. `transform`: nodes that create or change the answer's values. `good` / `warn` / `fail`: diagnostic status. One scheme per result.

node_ids.description: Node IDs that share this graph role or status.

highlight_groups.description: At least one group. For a single-object result, use color "target" on that object.

label.description: What the section's nodes share, as heading and badge (30 chars). No object names.

node_ids.description: Nodes this section documents; put each node in one section. Empty array when it documents none.

text.description: Required detail body for this section label.

sections.description: Report sections, at least one. Each section explains the node_ids it lists.

node_id.description: Node ID the caption sits below.

caption.description: One-sentence caption grounded in tool results.

scope_id.description: scope_id returned by lineage_get_scope_bundle: draws that scope as a new view. Send exactly one of scope_id and view_id.

view_id.description: view_id returned by an earlier lineage_present_result: edits that view, for example with prune_node_ids or add_node_ids.

languageModelTools.name: lineage_get_object_detail
languageModelTools.userDescription: Get full details for a specific database object.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Primary single-object lookup. Use this when the user asks about one specific object (DDL, columns, direct neighbors). For graph-scope lineage questions, prefer lineage_get_scope_bundle instead of chaining repeated per-node detail calls.

id.description: Canonical object ID returned by a lineage search or scope tool.

cursor.description: Page cursor: the next_cursor of the previous result, sent unchanged to read the next page of the same list. Omit for the first page.

languageModelTools.name: lineage_detect_graph_patterns
languageModelTools.userDescription: Find structural patterns like hubs, cycles, or orphans in the graph.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Analyzes the entire graph for specific structural patterns such as hubs, islands, orphans, longest paths, cycles, or external references.

min_degree.description: Minimum node degree for hub detection.

max_size.description: Maximum number of pattern results to return.

languageModelTools.name: lineage_search_ddl
languageModelTools.userDescription: Search SQL body scripts for a text pattern.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Grep view, procedure and function bodies. Each hit has object, line, matched line, context, `commented: true` when the match sits in a SQL comment, and `enclosing_predicate` with the governing IF/WHILE condition when the match is inside one. `by_object` is the per-object hit count. No matches is `total: 0`; a bad pattern is `invalid_regex` with the repair. Use lineage_search_objects for names.

query.description: Regular expression against SQL body text; case-insensitive; `^` and `$` match per line.

types.description: Optional body-type filter; omit to search all three.

languageModelTools.name: lineage_get_screen_state
languageModelTools.userDescription: Shows what is currently on screen: active trace, analysis, or applied bookmark.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns what is on screen: active trace, graph analysis, applied bookmark, and view. Optional `ids` recall objects from a stored AI run; optional `filter` lists pruned, open_leads, or stale. `ids` and `filter` need a stored run; without one they answer `no_run_memory`. Omit input for the screen card.

ids.description: Canonical object ids to recall from the stored run, taken from the screen card's node_ids. Use without filter.

filter.description: One class of the stored run to list: pruned, open_leads, or stale. Use without ids.

cursor.description: Page cursor: the next_cursor of the previous result, sent unchanged to read the next page of the same list. Omit for the first page.
